newsitem.title: USA: Florida referendum would end Tallahassee authority.
newsitem.headline: Florida referendum would end Tallahassee authority.

text.p: Property owners in Tallahassee, Fla., have submitted petitions calling for a vote to dissolve the city's Downtown Improvement Authority, The Tallahassee Democrat reported Wednesday.

The proposal would end the one-mill tax on downtown property, which raised $96,000 last year. Property owners complained that $86,000 of that went toward rent, office supplies and the salaries of its director and a part-time worker, rather than improvement projects.
The authority was created by the Legislature in 1971 to help revitalize the city's centeral business district as new shopping malls opened in the suburbs.
Dennis Murphy, a property owner who helped lead the petition drive, said the authority was never intended to last in perpetuity and does not raise enough money to support needed projects.

He delivered petitions signed by 30 property owners, representing 46 percent of the city's privately owned downtown real estate. Under state law, signatures of owners representing only 20 percent of the property are needed to call a referendum.
The city has 120 days to identify the property owners, deliver mail-in ballots and tally the votes.
